## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

##Part A
#Question 1
#a. Create a vector for the workers' ages.
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29,
         35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49,
         50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51,
         35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41,
         48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
#b. How many data points?
length(age)
#c. Find the minimum and maximum values.
min(age)
max(age)
#d. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33rd to 35th elements.
age[c(13:18, 33:35)]
#e. Access all elements except the 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th.
age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
#f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements to 0.
age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
age

##Question 2
data(rivers)

#Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
river_stats <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum = sum(rivers),
  mean = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  variance = var(rivers),
  standard_deviation = sd(rivers),
  minimum = min(rivers),
  maximum = max(rivers)
)

#What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
river_stats
